description: Language neutral sequences of the OFREP behaviour of the relay that need time: a store that changes, relays that follow it (one can be held back), a change stream. A sequence declares the flag documents it publishes, the relays that follow the store (default: one relay named a that polls every second), the flag sets of the first generation, and steps. Steps: request (relay, key sent as X-API-Key, context by name, single flag key or the bulk evaluation, query parameters, ifNoneMatch, save the response as a variable, eventually: repeat until the expectation holds, then assert it), publish (the next generation of the store), connect (open the flag change stream that a bulk response advertises), event (the next refetchEvaluation event of a stream, saved as a variable). Variables: $name is the ETag of a saved response, $name.etag and $name.lastModified are the fields of a saved event. Expectations: status, etag (present, same:name, differs:name), emptyBody, values (flag key to value), absent (flag keys that must not be in the bulk response), noValue (flags with no value), reasons, errorCode, eventStreams (url: one entry of type sse with a url and no endpoint), metadata (absent: no response level metadata), flagMetadata (flag key to the metadata entries it must contain). source: spec (the pinned document or ADR-0008), provider (an official provider relies on it), relay (behaviour neither defines); basis says why.

sequences.name: bulk ETag: the same context twice, and If-None-Match
sequences.basis: bulkEvaluation 200 ETag: entity tag of the current state of all flags, sent back in If-None-Match; 304: the ETag matches, no body

sequences.name: bulk ETag: a flag value changed and published
sequences.basis: the ETag represents the current state of the flags: a changed value is a new state, the old tag no longer validates

sequences.name: bulk ETag: a change that cannot affect the result of this context keeps the tag
sequences.basis: the ETag is the hash of the response body, so it changes if and only if the result for the context changes; a rule change for another plan does not change a free user's result

sequences.name: bulk ETag: a change outside the requested flag list keeps the tag
sequences.basis: the tag follows the response body: a bulk request for a list of flags does not change when another flag is removed

sequences.name: bulk ETag: another flag set changing, and a reload with no change for this one
sequences.basis: a generation that changes flag set b only leaves the configuration of flag set a, and so its tag, as it was

sequences.name: bulk ETag: a tag of one context never validates another context whose result differs
sequences.basis: 304 only when the ETag matches the current state of what this request would return

sequences.name: bulk ETag: a disabled flag, and a removed flag
sequences.basis: a disabled flag has the reason DISABLED and no value; both are new states of the flags

sequences.name: flag sets are isolated, single and bulk
sequences.basis: a key reaches the flags of its flag set only; an unknown flag is 404 FLAG_NOT_FOUND; 401 for credentials that do not authenticate, 403 for a key that may not evaluate

sequences.name: a replica that is behind answers a change-triggered refetch from the new configuration
sequences.basis: ADR-0008: flagConfigEtag and flagConfigLastModified carry what the change notification said and are sent only on a refetch it triggered, for server side cache validation and freshness; the JavaScript providers send them with If-None-Match

sequences.name: a replica that is behind, notified with the date only
sequences.basis: flagConfigLastModified is sent alone when the notification had no etag; the replica compares it with the date it built its configuration

sequences.name: a made up configuration identity is answered with what the relay has
sequences.basis: the parameters are hints: an identity the relay never loads is never an error, and the answer is the current configuration

sequences.name: the event stream loop: connect, change, notification, refetch
sequences.basis: the OFREP providers read eventStreams from the bulk response, connect to the url, and refetch with flagConfigEtag and flagConfigLastModified when a refetchEvaluation event arrives

sequences.name: response level and flag metadata
sequences.basis: bulkEvaluationSuccess.metadata is optional metadata of the flag set; the flag metadata is a map of booleans, strings and numbers; the relay has no flag set metadata to send
